libraryName: Expungement.ai + RCAP Master Forms and Legal-Review Library

retention.note: The user retained the Batch 1 authority archives outside this repository, and Edition 1.1 is published alongside them. This repository ignores *.zip and keeps record-clearing source corpora out of version control, so the edition is adopted in place and pinned by SHA-256 rather than copied in. The ZIP itself is the immutable authority artifact; it is read by temporary extraction or entry streaming and is never re-committed, re-packed or relocated. An extracted tree at the same path is read in place instead, with no second copy created.

immutableEditionRule: Every published edition is immutable. No file inside an adopted edition is edited, moved, renamed, re-hashed or supplemented by this repository, and a published archive is never rebuilt in place — a changed archive is a different edition, not a correction. A newer law, official revision, post-cutoff acquisition or correction enters through: current edition -> pending amendment -> reviewed and adopted new edition -> repository remapping. Edition 1.0 and Edition 1.1 are both retained and independently verifiable.
authorityPrecedence: 1. The current adopted Master Library edition.
2. The adopted legal-resolution memorandum retained inside that edition, where it changes legal structure, output strategy, packet capability, product scope, blocker treatment or node classification.
3. The jurisdiction legal review retained inside that edition, for conclusions the adopted memorandum does not change.
4. The Master Asset Manifest, state manifests, missing/source-gap ledger, exclusion log, duplicate log and checksums, for source identity and asset treatment.
5. Normalized legal-design records and application registries, as derived implementation outputs.
resolverSelectionRule: A packet resolver may select an asset only through an explicit approved mapping from a normalized legal-design component to one retained Master Library asset, matched by workflow key or document ID with a matching SHA-256, correct document role, correct language and an approved revision. Selection by filename, folder scan, directory listing, title similarity or file presence is prohibited. A source_gated, excluded, retired, superseded or unmanifested asset is never resolver-selectable. Edition 1.1 sets generation_allowed = no on all 394 retained assets, so no asset is resolver-selectable under Edition 1.1 alone.
filePresenceRule: A binary existing in the Master Library, this repository, a prior source folder, a legal-review package or an imported archive is not source approval and does not make an asset runtime-ready.
sharedAssetRule: A form used by several tracks is one canonical source asset with several explicit track mappings. The binary is not duplicated per track, and a track ID never appears in a canonical filename.
thirdPartyFieldRule: Judge, clerk, prosecutor, law-enforcement, agency, notary and process-server fields remain blank unless the governing form expressly assigns the field to the participant.
derivedRecordRule: The files above are derived application records that point at the adopted edition. They are regenerated by `npm run rcap:reconcile-master-library` and are never hand-edited to change a source's status. The Master Library is not copied into this directory.

parentEdition.note: Edition 1.0 remains unmodified and separately hashable. Edition 1.1 inherits all 378 of its canonical assets unchanged; it does not replace or edit it.

sourceArchives.treatment: Controlling Batch 1 authority. Its twelve amended state reviews become the active canonical legal-review assets; its packet-only amendment, decision matrix and 117-track crosswalk become governance authority under 00_GOVERNANCE/BATCH_1_AUTHORITY/.

Provenance baseline only. Its twelve original reviews are recorded in the exclusion/reference log with their hashes and are NOT published as a second set of active controlling reviews and NOT counted as legal-review authorities. All twelve were confirmed preserved verbatim beneath their state addendum in the amended review.

batch1ControllingPrecedence: 1. The state-specific controlling addendum at the beginning of the amended state review.
4. The original state review preserved beneath the state addendum.
5. 00_GOVERNANCE/BATCH_1_AUTHORITY/pre-amendment-crosswalk/ only as a completeness inventory and crosswalk, never as final legal truth.
reviewAuthorityIsNotReadiness: A retained controlling legal review satisfies legal-review identity for a jurisdiction. It does not satisfy track-source mapping, clear a form, establish source currentness, or resolve a conflict between the 117-track authority crosswalk and the current normalization. Those remain separate, separately-counted gates.
resolutionOrder: 1. An explicit path supplied by the caller (CLI --library=).
4. Fail closed. The repository source corpus is never a fallback.

batch1AmendedNormalizationApplied.note: Per jurisdiction, not global. A jurisdiction is marked applied only when all of its authoritative source IDs are accounted exactly once, its live tracks are confirmed against the controlling amended addendum, and its deferred true blockers are represented as deferred source slots. Marking a jurisdiction applied closes the broad jurisdiction-level reconciliation gate only; every track-level blocker the controlling review retains stays open and continues to fail closed.

batch1AmendedNormalizationRule: Edition 1.1 adopted twelve amended Batch 1 reviews as controlling authority after those jurisdictions were normalized. The bounded amended-normalization pass has now read the 117-track authority crosswalk against the live registry jurisdiction by jurisdiction, so the twelve jurisdiction-level reconciliation gates are cleared. Clearing a jurisdiction gate is not clearance of its tracks: the seven deferred source IDs remain deferred true blockers, and any track whose controlling review retains an open legal-design blocker still fails closed on that blocker.
